run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation pods and their gRPC/DB dependencies all started cleanly in the 30 seconds before the window ended: 19/19 pods Running and ready with restartCount 0, all seven backends registered themselves in consul between 09:40:03Z and 09:40:11Z, and a trace sample at 09:40:28Z shows HTTP 200 on /hotels and /reservation with successful search, geo, rate, profile, recommendation, user and reservation client spans. The concrete defect the evidence shows is a routing misconfiguration around the app's entry-point Service: the live `frontend` Service selector is {service-route: frontend} while its own last-applied configuration records {io.kompose.service: frontend}, and exactly two pods carry service-route=frontend -- the frontend pod and the search pod. The frontend Endpoints therefore list 10.244.125.25 (the search pod) on port 5000, although the search container only listens on 8082/9092. The search Deployment's pod template gained that label in a rollout at 09:40:10-09:40:11Z (ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 without the label replaced by search-9cd459687 with it). Because metrics stop at 09:40:29Z, the frontend container logs no per-request lines, there is no in-cluster load generator, and the single blackbox probe after both labelled pods existed succeeded, the resulting client-visible failure rate is a hypothesis, not a measured impact. The pre-staged Mongo privilege-revocation tooling (ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate mounted into mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate) was checked and rejected as the active cause for this window: both mongod instances authenticated the admin user and served reads, and their logs show no authorization failures.

claims.text: All 19 pods in namespace hotel-reservation were Running with every container ready and restartCount 0, including frontend-5566ddfbfb-hhrhw, search-9cd459687-xz4hq, geo-d4c78b89b-bhl99, rate-65d6967c95-9r45x, profile-7f5f54c8-28h94, recommendation-86cf75495d-hx66t, reservation-7d77c6cb59-cmt7s, user-5ccf6db68f-d769n and the mongodb-* / memcached-* pods.

The `frontend` Service's live spec.selector is {"service-route":"frontend"}, while the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation on the same object records selector {"io.kompose.service":"frontend"}; the `search` Service's selector is still {"io.kompose.service":"search"}.
Only two pods carry the label service-route=frontend: frontend-5566ddfbfb-hhrhw (pod IP 10.244.7.236) and search-9cd459687-xz4hq (pod IP 10.244.125.25); no other Service selects on service-route.

The `frontend` Endpoints object publishes two ready addresses on port 5000, 10.244.7.236 and 10.244.125.25, and 10.244.125.25 is also the only address of the `search` Endpoints object and the address the search pod registered in consul (10.244.125.25:8082), i.e. the search pod.

The search container hotel-reserv-search declares only containerPort 8082 and 9092 (named metrics), while the `frontend` Service exposes port 5000 with targetPort 5000, so the search pod has no listener on the port it is published on as a frontend endpoint.

The search Deployment's pod template gained the label service-route: frontend during a rollout: ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 (labels only io.kompose.service=search) was replaced by search-9cd459687 (labels io.kompose.service=search plus service-route=frontend), with events 'Scaled up replica set search-9cd459687 from 0 to 1' at 09:40:10Z and 'Scaled down replica set search-567bb6c4b8 from 1 to 0' at 09:40:11Z; the frontend Deployment was rolled out the same way (frontend-68745cb99c without the label to frontend-5566ddfbfb with it, 09:40:08Z-09:40:10Z).

The blackbox gRPC probe of the frontend Service (instance frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, job blackbox-hotel-reservation) reported probe_success=0 at the 09:39:29Z and 09:39:59Z samples and probe_success=1 at the 09:40:29Z sample; the same probe for rate:8084 and recommendation:8085 also turned 1 at 09:40:29Z.

Every backend registered itself in consul during startup (srv-recommendation 09:40:03Z, srv-rate 09:40:04Z, srv-geo 09:40:05Z, srv-reservation 09:40:07Z, srv-user 09:40:08Z, srv-profile 09:40:09Z, srv-search 09:40:11Z) and the service logs contained no rpc error / Unavailable / deadline / connection-refused lines in 09:40:00Z-09:40:29Z.

A trace sample taken at 09:40:28Z shows requests that reached the frontend pod completing successfully: HTTP GET /hotels and HTTP POST /reservation carry http.status_code 200, and the client spans /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations, /user.User/CheckUser and /reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation carry no error status (status_state not_recorded for most of them).

Database fault-injection tooling is pre-staged in the namespace: ConfigMap failure-admin-geo holds revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh and remove-admin-mongo.sh that revoke/restore the readWrite role on database geo-db, ConfigMap failure-admin-rate holds the equivalent scripts for rate-db, and Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate mount these ConfigMaps as volume 'failure-script' (mounted at /scripts in the mongo containers).

No evidence that those privilege-revocation scripts took effect: mongodb-geo logged 'Authentication succeeded' for principal admin at 09:40:05Z and created/indexed collection geo-db.geo, the geo service logged a successful DB session plus test-data generation and started serving, and filtered reads of the mongodb-geo log (read through 09:41:04Z) and the mongodb-rate log (read through 09:42:03Z) returned no revoke / grantRoles / not-authorized / authentication-failed lines.

The fault the evidence supports is that the entry-point Service `frontend` load-balances to a pod that does not serve it: its selector service-route=frontend matches both the frontend pod and the search pod, so a share of TCP connections to frontend:5000 are delivered to search-9cd459687-xz4hq, which only listens on 8082/9092 and would refuse port 5000. That mechanism is consistent with the two failed frontend probe samples at 09:39:29Z and 09:39:59Z while all pods reported ready.

The change most likely injected is the service-route: frontend label added to the search Deployment's pod template during the 09:40:10Z-09:40:11Z rollout, which made the search pod a second endpoint of the frontend Service; because the same label was also added to the frontend template and the Service selector was changed to match, I cannot rule out that the Service selector change is the primary defect instead.

The frontend Service was reachable in the last sample (probe_success=1 for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 at 09:40:29Z) and the 09:40:28Z trace sample contains only successful HTTP 200 responses, so no observed request actually failed inside the sampled window; one probe sample cannot establish a failure rate for a Service that has one serving and one dead endpoint.

The ingress blackbox target http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=... reported probe_success=0 in every sampled point between 09:38:59Z and 09:40:29Z while the pods' own direct blackbox probes were recovering to 1, so that failure is not attributable to the application's own services on the evidence available.

Revoked MongoDB admin privileges on geo-db or rate-db (the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts) was considered as the active fault and rejected for the sampled window: mongodb-geo authenticated the admin principal and served geo reads/writes, the geo service started normally on that connection, the rate- and geo-backed gRPC calls in the 09:40:28Z trace sample carried no error status, and neither mongod log shows authorization failures.

Verify and correct the frontend Service routing: either restore the frontend Service selector to a label only the frontend pod carries (the selector in its own last-applied configuration, io.kompose.service=frontend) or remove service-route: frontend from the search Deployment template, then confirm that the frontend Endpoints list only the frontend pod IP on port 5000.

gaps: No baseline and almost no runtime window: every application pod was created between 2026-11-21T09:39:53Z and 09:40:11Z, i.e. 18-36 seconds before the authorized window ended, and Prometheus samples stop at 2026-11-21T09:40:29Z, so no pre-incident comparison of frontend routing or request success rates exists.

The failure rate produced by the bad frontend endpoint is unmeasured: the frontend container logs only startup lines (31 lines, 09:40:09Z), no request-level errors were captured, and there is no in-cluster load generator (a cluster-wide pod query selected nothing matching load/locust/generator/chaos/inject/probe, result_count 0).

The query for Ingress objects returned nothing, and a pod query filtered to namespaces matching ingress/observe returned only observe-namespace pods; since an empty result shows only that the query matched nothing, whether an ingress controller exists and whether the failing ingress blackbox target could ever reach the app remains unchecked rather than established.

No spanmetrics series had samples in the window: get_metric_names showed traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_* exist under job otel-spanmetrics, but instant and range queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned nothing, and the application series rate_* / search_* returned no samples for the whole window, so per-operation error and latency rates could not be computed.

Nothing records who or what changed the frontend Service selector and the frontend/search pod templates, or exactly when; the change_history integration is not available in this Run, and Kubernetes objects were read at ~09:42-09:43Z, after the window end, so their state during the window is only partly inferable from ReplicaSet templates and events.

Whether the pre-staged failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts were ever executed cannot be verified: exec sessions are not visible, the scripts' output does not appear in container stdout, and Kubernetes events do not record exec calls.
Secret values were not readable, so the root/admin credentials referenced by the failure scripts could not be verified against the running databases.
Kafka was not consulted and forms no part of this application's architecture; no Kafka-related symptom appeared in the evidence reviewed.
next_steps: Check the deployment/change tooling that produced the 09:40:08Z-09:40:11Z rollouts to determine whether labelling the search Deployment with service-route: frontend was intentional; if not, treat it as the injected change.

Measure frontend Service success rate over a longer window with a client that records TCP-level failures, or add a probe that targets the frontend pod directly, to quantify how many connections land on the search pod's unopened port 5000.

Confirm the intended selector for the frontend Service in source (its last-applied configuration shows io.kompose.service: frontend) and check whether any other workload depends on service-route labels.

If DB privilege revocation is suspected in a later window, re-check mongod authorization logs and geo/rate service error logs for 'not authorized on geo-db/rate-db' after real traffic has run, since the pre-staged scripts exist but showed no effect in this window.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
